original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. WE induces the transactivation of PPARα and directly binds to and activates PPARα. (A) Luciferase assay. The pSG5-PPARα and pCMV-3xPPRE-Luc constructs were co-transfected into CHO-K1 cells, and the cells were treated with WE (10, 50, 100, or 500 μM) or GW7647 (1 μM) for 24 h. WE and GW7647 activate PPARα transactivation. (B) WE (10^-3–10^7 nM) or GW7647 (10^-4–10^5 nM) were incubated with the PPARα LBD protein and the co-activator (PGC1α), and the treatment of WE and GW7647 induced the co-activator activity of the PPARα LBD as measured by a TR-FRET co-activator assay. (C) WE (C, left) and GW7647 (C, right) directly bind the PPARα LBD protein as measured by a SPR assay. (D) Molecular docking of WE to the PPARα LBD. The data are presented as the mean ± SEM, and significant differences were calculated using a one-way ANOVA test. Different letters indicate significant differences between the groups.

original_paragraph.Results section: WE is a PPARα ligand: Hepatic steatosis is mainly caused by TG accumulation in the liver, which is induced by increased hepatic fatty acid synthesis and/or decreased β-oxidation.21 PPARα regulates the expression of several genes involved in hepatic fatty acid metabolism, and we hypothesized that the dipeptide WE functions as a PPARα agonist that reduces intracellular lipid concentrations in hepatocytes. In the reporter gene assay performed as described previously,22,23 WE stimulated the transactivation of PPARα by 53% and 62% at 100 and 500 μM, respectively, whereas the PPARα agonist GW7647 (1 μM) induced PPARα transactivation by 98% (Fig. 3A). The agonistic activities of WE and PPARα were examined with TR-FRET analyses using the PPARα co-activator PGC1α as described previously23 (Fig. 3B). WE activated PPARα with a half maximal effective concentration (EC50) of 83.4 μM (Table 1). Direct binding of WE to the PPARα LBD protein was further tested by a SPR-Biacore assay as described previously23 (Fig. 3C). WE directly associated with the PPARα LBD protein, and the Kd of this interaction was 120 μM; GW7647 also bound the PPARα LBD protein (with a Kd value of 96.4 nM) (Table 1). The binding modeling assay of WE to PPARα protein24 showed that WE bound to PPARα through hydrogen bonding via its hydroxyl and amino groups either Glu286, Asn219 or Met220 (Fig. 3D). These results indicate that WE directly binds to PPARα and induces conformational changes to recruit a coactivator peptide, thus increasing PPARα transactivation.
